_what_this_is: DRAFT starter values for kits/weathering/sets/japanese_courtyard.json, written from the study '12b Second set - the Japanese courtyard.md'. The key names are a PROPOSAL (the kit's schema is not built yet); every number comes from the saved scene or the build script, or is marked GUESS. Nothing in the kit code should repeat any of this.

roles._how_to_read: A role is a kind of surface. Each role lists how to find its objects or materials. Lists are tried in order; first rule that matches wins. 'material_props' reads a custom property the add-on writes on its own materials.

ground.earth.note: material 'Moss and earth' (noise colour + bump). The add-on's moss clumps and pebbles sit on it.

ground.gravel.note: 31,486 faces, rake lines are real 1.6 cm relief; weathering must not flatten them. Bounds x 0.9..9.1, y -5.9..1.9.

growth.existing.note: real geometry already grown by the add-on: 32,365 moss faces, 5,654 pebble faces. Treated as a density picture the kit moss must not double.

stone.natural.note: 42 separate add-on materials, one per stone, each a 'FOUNDRY / Wet Stone' group with no Principled box on the surface: needs the adapter. Stones are 61-72 faces after the add-on's modifiers.

stone.dressed.note: plain noise material 'Plinth stone'. The plinth is a 10.9 x 5.6 m slab, top at z 0.55.

timber.deck.note: 8 plank runs: .000-.002 = veranda (planks run along y, 1.8 m), .003-.007 = bridge (planks run across, 1.05 m). One plain Principled material per tone, no grain in the material; grain direction must come from the mesh.

timber.frame.note: 'Dark timber' and 'Beam timber' noise materials; posts stand on the deck at z 0.55; lattice bars are 2.8 cm.

roof.tile.note: geometry nodes: the base mesh has 42 faces (timber deck + ridge); the tiles are 688 INSTANCES of one hidden 12-face tile (0.30 x 0.66 x 0.22 m). Layers must read the surface in the shader or work on a realised copy.

wall.plaster.note: 'Plaster wall' noise material; boxes of 6 faces; garden walls 0.3 m thick, 2.1-2.2 m tall.

wall.cap.note: 0.5 m wide dark tiled cap, 0.1 m overhang each side of the 0.3 m wall: the run-off source for the wall faces.

bamboo.note: leave alone in round one (not enough pixels: 0.5 % of the photo).

never_weather.note: 6 glow-only materials, 6 leaf-type materials (vertex colour, some with a see-through mix). 'CT / ' objects include a hidden tile prototype that carries the roof tile material: hook the MATERIAL, skip the OBJECT for any measuring.

ground_picture.note: ground height from a downward ray at each dot; the ground source object is hidden and must be skipped.

walls.frame: each wall is an axis-aligned box in world space (no turned copies, no shared meshes), so wall pictures can be made in world coordinates

sources.found_by: lowest up-facing edge of the evaluated roof, 0.3 m wide tile rows
sources.drops_to: ground and plinth in front of the hall
sources.note: front eave at about y 4.4, z 3.2; the drip line lands on the bank between pond and plinth (the Japanese 'amaochi')

sources.drops_to: both faces of each garden wall
Lantern gallery, firebox and post below
sources.note: 0.96 m wide cap over a 0.46 m firebox

water.note: the pond water is one big plane (8.2 x 6.2 m) lying just under the shore; the visible shore is where the GROUND crosses z -0.12. The water edge picture must come from the ground height picture and the level, not from the water object's outline. Pond centre (-3.0, 1.0), radii 3.3 x 2.5, turned 10 degrees; bank stones sit on the shore. Basin water is a 0.22 m disc on the water basin stone.

footfall.note: the walking strip along the front of the hall
raked, nobody walks on it: no footfall, only the stepping stones across it

existing_growth.note: the add-on grew moss from 7 hand-placed patches: front-left (-7.4,-3.0), hill (-8.2,6.0), maple root (-6.9,2.0), rocks (-3.4,4.0), lantern (1.0,1.4), gravel islands (5.9,-2.2), path edge (3.9,-3.3). In the study the add-on's moss matched year-round shade only weakly (rank match +0.15 over land).

shade_model.note: ASSUMPTION: the hall faces south (-y), the usual way for a hall looking over a garden, and the golden-hour sun low in the west (-x) fits that. The user should confirm. If the set has no real north, set 'mode' to 'declared' and give a shade-side vector.

cameras.name: Camera
cameras.note: the only camera in the scene; a plate for the film would be another camera (tall plate shape): list it here

plate.tested: 1200 x 800, 48 samples: 1.2 s on the rented card; the scene was built for Cycles but EEVEE draws it (see study)

add_on_groups.adapter: rebuild one Principled from the group's Albedo, Roughness and Normal outputs, copy the other plain numbers (Specular IOR Level 0.4, IOR 1.5 ...) from the Principled inside the group
add_on_groups.tested: 46 of 46 materials, picture identical in Cycles (0.0 largest difference in float), within one step of 255 on 0.8 % of dots in EEVEE

palette_from_the_scene.note: so that kit growth matches what is already there

plate_brightness_measured.note: mean brightness of each family in the 1200 x 800 EEVEE picture (0 black .. 1 white); share of dots under 0.13 is the zone the stage crushes
